quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Your tires grip the road less well as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires grip the road less well as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires cannot remove water as well when you go faster. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your car.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes ahead. Look for signals from other drivers. Cars will merge at on-ramps, and road conditions can change quickly.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm out. This law applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You may turn in that direction after stopping.
You may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
They brake slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you cannot stop in time if the motorcycle stops suddenly. You need enough space to avoid a crash.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let merging traffic in safely.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:
questions.explanation: Slow down for curves and other hazards. You can drive slower than the posted limit for safety, but never faster. Reduce speed for curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: You may park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Do not park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and walk for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. People are more likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. People are more likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be unsafe.

questions.question: You can use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when it is dark or visibility is poor.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them plenty of space.
Speed up and pull in front of the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, slow down and give them as much space as possible. Cyclists have less protection than car drivers and should not be crowded. Passing too fast can push the cyclist off course.

questions.question: Rumble strips are used to:

options.text: Alert tired or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road.
Show that a stop sign is ahead.
Help slow a vehicle with brake problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert tired or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips are bumps or ridges on the road edge. They make noise and vibrations to wake up inattentive drivers and warn them they are leaving their lane.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
Reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. If a new speed limit is shown on this sign, it begins right at the sign.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, you should:
questions.explanation: At dusk or on cloudy days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: In rain, you should be extra careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has rained all day.
About half an hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. At this time, oil from cars mixes with rain and makes the road very slippery.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to reduce the risk of hydroplaning. Driving too fast can make your tires float on water and lose grip with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction to drive on a one-way street. It is a regulation sign that controls how traffic must move.

questions.question: When you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: First, release the gas pedal to slow down on a slippery road. If you need to slow down more, gently press your brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep a distance of at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly, and following too closely is dangerous for both of you. If the motorcycle falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting the rider. This is especially important on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert and careful. Slow down as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: In fog, you should use your high beam headlights to see better.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights or fog lights instead. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass only from your direction.
No one can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.
